## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Jahatikathā* (Kv 1.5) is the fifth discourse of the first chapter of the *Kathāvatthu*, situated within the Abhidhamma Piṭaka of the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. Modern scholarship renders the title as the "discussion of renouncing," classifying it among the core controversial debates of the *Kathāvatthu* where the Sthaviravādin/Theravādin refutes the propositions of rival Buddhist schools through rigorous dialectical methods [Watanabe 1983]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation of the text and registers references or thematic parallels to several canonical discourses, including the *Dhammikasutta* (AN 6.54), the *Sattasūriyasutta* (AN 7.66), the *Mahāparinibbāna Sutta* (DN 16), and the *Anubuddhasutta* (AN 4.1) [SuttaCentral].
While SuttaCentral does not catalog curated external parallels, automated analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse (834 matches across 42 texts) [DharmaNexus]. The highest volume of reuse occurs with related debates in the *Kathāvatthu*, most notably the *Aparāpisamannāgatakathā* (Kv 4.9), *Sabbasaṁyojanappahānakathā* (Kv 4.10), *Anupubbābhisamayakathā* (Kv 2.9), *Ekamaggakathā* (Kv 18.5), and *Sabbamatthītikathā* (Kv 1.6), alongside canonical parallels in the *Sattakanipāta* (AN 7) and *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12) [DharmaNexus]. Cross-language alignments computed by DharmaNexus link the text with the Chinese translation of the *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100) and Tibetan translations of scholastic treatises, namely the *Abhidharmasamuccayavyākhyā* (D4054) and the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* (D4090-2) [DharmaNexus].
